# Probe notes — pass 1

Real tmux was driven on a throwaway socket (`tmux -L probe`) to de-risk the
requirements before spec-writing. Findings for the next pass:

## R2 — F5 generated by one run-shell loop: PROVEN

`run-shell`'s command argument IS format-expanded before it reaches the
shell — `#{pane_id}` inside it resolves immediately. Escape with `##{...}`
to get a literal `#{...}` into the generated `bind-key` call.

Chaining two commands onto one key from the CLI (the `\;` that works inside
tmux.conf's own parser) requires passing the two literal characters `\;` as
one argv token — a bare `;` (quoted or not) is read as a top-level command
separator by tmux's own client parser and runs the second `if-shell`
immediately instead of binding it. Working shell fragment, run from inside
`run-shell`, no other change needed:

```sh
i=1; letters="abcdefghi"
while [ "$i" -le 9 ]; do
    l=$(printf "%s" "$letters" | cut -c"$i")
    tmux bind-key -T jump "$i" if -F "##{m:*|$i|*,##{W:|##{window_index}|}}" \
        "select-window -t :$i" "new-window -t :$i -c ~" "\;" \
        if -F "##{==:##{window_panes},1}" "switch-client -T root" "switch-client -T jump-pane"
    tmux bind-key -T jump "$l" select-pane -t ":.$i"
    tmux bind-key -T jump-pane "$l" select-pane -t ":.$i"
    i=$((i + 1))
done
```

Verified against a real server: produces byte-identical `list-keys -T jump`
/ `list-keys -T jump-pane` output to the current 27 hand-written binds
(digits 1-9 chained correctly, letters a-i in both tables). No `-L probe`
in the real file — inside a running session the bare `tmux` on PATH picks
up the session's own socket via `$TMUX`.

# Probe notes — pass 2 (resumed after pass 1 was cut off mid-probe)

Pass 1's "Not yet built" section above is **stale**. Between 14:23 and 14:32
that pass wrote R1 (partly), R2, R5 (partly), R6 and R7 into the live files
and was cut off before it could say so. Everything below is pass 2 continuing
from that tree.

## The thing pass 1 died on: a popup needs an attached client

`tmux new-session -d` leaves a server with NO attached client, and
`display-popup` is refused there. So the F3 binding read as broken on the one
harness that is convenient to reach for. `list-keys` proves the binding
parsed and proves nothing about whether it dispatches.

`f3-verify.py` is the harness that works: `pty.fork()`, `tmux -f <conf>
new-session` in the child, the real escape sequence written to the master
(`\x1bOR` for F3, `\x1b[1;2R` for Shift+F3), and the bound command touching a
file to record that it ran. `capture-pane` does NOT capture the status line,
so detecting a binding with `display-message` reads as a failure that is not
one — that cost one round.

## The defect it exposed: `display-popup -e` is never format-expanded

`-d '#{E:@cwd}'` IS expanded. `-e 'TV_ALL_ORIGIN=#{pane_id}'` is NOT — the
twelve literal characters reach the popup's environment, and `tv-all`'s
`split-window -t "$ORIGIN"` then has no pane to open against. Measured three
ways (`f3-dispatch2.py`, `f3-dispatch4.py`, `f3-dispatch5.py`): as the direct
argument of a key binding, inside a `command-prompt` template, and through
`run-shell`. Only `run-shell` produced a real pane id, because it is
`run-shell` doing the expansion on its own argument — the same rule R2's
generated `bind-key` loop leans on.

**This is not a defect R7 introduced.** `f3-dispatch4.py` test 1 reproduces it
against HEAD's own shape, the two-popup binding that has been on the desk all
along. It has always been broken; nothing measured it until now.

## The fix, and why the obvious spellings do not work

`f3-dispatch5.py` tried four spellings written the way they would appear in
`tmux.conf` and sourced from a file. Only one dispatches:

```tmux
bind -n F3 command-prompt -p 'search' {
    run-shell "tmux display-popup -E -B -w 90% -h 85% -x C -y C -d '#{E:@cwd}' -e 'TV_ALL_ORIGIN=#{pane_id}' '~/.local/bin/tv-all here %1'"
}
```

The `{}` block matters as much as the `run-shell`: a backslash-continued
quoted template carrying the same text parses without error and then silently
never fires (`f3-dispatch4.py` test 2). The three that failed, for the record,
were the popup shell resolving the origin itself with `$(tmux display -p …)`,
the same with `##{}` escaping, and `set -gF @f3origin "#{pane_id}"` read back
with `show -gv` — all three parse and none dispatch.

`f3-verify.py` now passes, twice, exit 0 twice: F3 prompts, a query reaches
`tv-all` with the real origin pane and the pane's cwd, Shift+F3 reaches the
everywhere lane, and Escape runs nothing and leaves nothing on screen.

## What pass 2 also cut, and re-loaded clean

R3 (the `c` widen cycle and `@copy-cycle`, out of `tmux.conf`), R4 (the
Claude-pane counter out of `status-left`, the per-pane loop out of
`status-format[1]`, the busy-window loop out of `window-status-format`), the
rest of R5 (`pbcopy` as the only sink, one `@host` arm, one `colors.conf`
source), and R9's two `capsule` keys out of `wezterm.lua`. The config loads,
`list-keys -T jump` is still 27, `copy-mode-vi` has no `c`, and
`wezterm --config-file … ls-fonts` parses.
